_schema.purpose: Registry of source-level facts that are properties of the SOURCE rather than of any particular fetch. Resolved at build time by scripts/build/project_candidates.py, so correcting an entry here never requires re-downloading a dump.

fields.source_available_at: ISO date the source dataset or site first became publicly available. Gates whether a player at a given in-game date could plausibly have this source as a tool. Null means ungated.
fields.confidence: high = first-party or multiple independent sources agree on a specific date; medium = single credible secondary source, or month known but not day; low = inferred.
fields.evidence: What was actually read, with the URL. A date with no evidence entry is not permitted.
fields.corpus_start: Earliest content the source covers, where different from source_available_at.

_schema.policy: Never guess a date. A fabricated clock is indistinguishable from a real one later and silently corrupts the in-game gating mechanic. Leave null and record the attempt.

epoch_ai.name: Epoch AI, Data on Notable AI Models

evidence.claim: Epoch AI's data hub, including the public model database, launched in June 2024. Epoch AI itself was founded June 2022.
evidence.via: web search summary of first-party pages

epoch_ai.notes: Day unknown; pinned to month start. Predecessor datasets on compute trends existed from approximately 2022 (Sevilla et al., Compute Trends Across Three Eras of Machine Learning), so an earlier gate could be argued for compute data specifically. Single-sourced -- worth a first-party confirmation before the gating mechanic ships.

forum_lesswrong.name: LessWrong

evidence.claim: In early March 2009, Yudkowsky founded LessWrong, repurposing his contributions to Overcoming Bias as seed content.
evidence.via: first-party site history post, corroborated by Wikipedia

evidence.claim: LessWrong 2.0 open beta began 2017-09-20; full launch March 2018.

forum_lesswrong.notes: Two defensible gates. Site readability by a player dates from 2009-03 and is what source_available_at records. The GraphQL API this repo actually uses only exists from LessWrong 2.0 (2017-09-20), which matters for reproducibility but not for in-game knowledge gating. Predecessor Overcoming Bias launched November 2006.

forum_eaforum.name: EA Forum

evidence.claim: The EA Forum launched in 2014, with seed content from a group blog that ran between 2012 and 2014. A newer version launched in 2018 on a new codebase.

forum_eaforum.notes: Year known, month not. Pinned to year start, which biases the gate EARLY by up to eleven months. If the gating mechanic proves sensitive to this, pin down the month before relying on it.

openalex.name: OpenAlex

evidence.claim: OpenAlex was released on 1 January 2022 by OurResearch as a replacement for Microsoft Academic Graph, which Microsoft retired at the end of 2021.

openalex.notes: Adapter not yet written. Predecessor Microsoft Academic Graph was available from approximately 2015 to 2021-12-31, so scholarly-graph tooling as a capability predates OpenAlex itself.

arxiv.name: arXiv

evidence.claim: arXiv was founded by Paul Ginsparg in 1991.

arxiv.notes: Year is first-party confirmed; the MONTH is not. August 1991 is widely cited (hep-th began then) but the About page states only the year, so the date is pinned to 1991-08-01 with the month unverified. Metadata licensing varies by paper; per-paper licence must be checked if full text is ever retained.

aiid.name: AI Incident Database

evidence.claim: The AI Incident Database launched publicly in November 2020 via Partnership on AI, announced by Sean McGregor on 2020-11-18.
evidence.via: Partnership on AI announcement plus contemporaneous mailing list post

aiid.notes: NOT INGESTED. Reuse terms are not stated on the snapshots page and could not be confirmed as CC-BY compatible, so this source is excluded under the repo's CC-BY-4.0 posture until terms are established. Snapshot route if terms clear: weekly tar.bz2 at the R2 bucket linked from incidentdatabase.ai/research/snapshots/.

mit_airr.name: MIT AI Risk Repository

evidence.claim: Site states: Data from the MIT AI Risk Initiative is licensed under CC BY 4.0.
Repository published with Slattery et al. 2024, arXiv:2408.12622, August 2024.

mit_airr.notes: Adapter landed 2026-07-25 (scripts/adapters/mit_airr.py); this is the tagging spine. Licence additionally confirmed inside the workbook itself. Day unknown, pinned to month start. Database access via Google Sheets copy link and OneDrive mirror linked from the /risks page. Now also published in Patterns (2026). The initiative additionally hosts an AI Incident Tracker, an AI Governance database, and expert survey results under the same licence -- all unexplored.

sff.name: Survival and Flourishing Fund

evidence.claim: Per-round recommendation pages are published from 2019 through 2026. The 2019 page describes itself as covering 2019-Q4. Nine rounds parsed to 324 grant rows totalling USD 75,101,415; four later pages could not be parsed by the same code and are NOT known to be empty.
evidence.via: direct HTTP probe and table parse from the Windows seat

evidence.claim: The source states that recommendations may not become disbursements: some grants might not happen if they are logistically difficult or time-consuming for the Funders.

sff.notes: NOT INGESTED. Reuse terms not located, so license_spdx is null and no dump may be published until confirmed. Publishes RECOMMENDATIONS, not disbursements: store recommended_usd, never amount (ADR-009 s3). Rounds are jointly funded -- 2019 names Jaan Tallinn (independent) alongside SFF -- so the column is not attributable to SFF alone. Markup changed after 2023-H2 from table/td to div class=in-grid (673 divs, 618 dollar amounts on the 2025 page), so one parser will silently return zero rows for 2024 onward. Pages are UTF-8 with curly quotes; decode explicitly or reproduce #68. See #94.

manifund.name: Manifund

evidence.claim: api/v0/projects returns HTTP 200 without a key or account, 100 records per page, paginated by a before cursor. A probe with before=2024-01-01 returned projects created 2023-12-30, so history reaches at least that far back. Earlier bound not probed.
evidence.via: direct HTTP probe from the Windows seat

evidence.claim: Stated and moved money differ by 18x. The newest 100 projects on this date sum to USD 9,039,076 of funding_goal and USD 502,800 of txns, with 9 of 100 projects carrying any transaction and 90 at stage proposal.
evidence.via: local computation over the fetched payload

manifund.notes: NOT INGESTED. Reuse terms not checked. Carries a native cause taxonomy usable for AI-safety filtering: tais (Technical AI safety), ai-gov, gcr, forecasting, biosec. Never sum funding_goal and call it funding (ADR-009 s3). RELATED PARTY: Pip has a live Manifund campaign, ruled 2026-08-22 to be INCLUDED and flagged with related_party true rather than silently excluded (ADR-009 s5).

metaculus.name: Metaculus

evidence.claim: The API is token-gated, not bot-blocked. An unauthenticated request returns HTTP 403 with the body: Permission Error: The API is only available to authenticated users. Please create an account and use your API token to access the API.
evidence.via: direct HTTP probe from the Windows seat, browser user-agent, redirects followed

metaculus.notes: NOT INGESTED. Would be the FIRST credentialed source in this repo: no adapter currently reads a token (grep getenv|API_KEY|TOKEN over scripts/adapters/ returns nothing). Requires a CI secret and must not re-arm either de-armed committing workflow. A community forecast is an attributed published number, so it is a fact about an opinion and permitted under ADR-001. Note coordination/forecasts/register.jsonl already holds the same record shape (statement, p, criterion, resolves_on, outcome) and the two want one schema.

coefficient_giving.name: Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy)

evidence.claim: Open Philanthropy renamed to Coefficient Giving in November 2025 and restructured into 13 cause-specific funds. openphilanthropy.org/grants/ now returns 301 to coefficientgiving.org/funds/.
evidence.via: redirect chain observed directly, corroborated by web search of first-party and trade-press pages

evidence.claim: No machine-readable grants feed located. The site is WordPress with 309 wp-json routes and none is a grant post type; the sitemap indexes page, careers, research, team, content-type and focus-area only; /grants is Algolia-backed and returns 403 to non-browser fetchers.
evidence.via: direct HTTP probe and route enumeration from the Windows seat

coefficient_giving.notes: NOT INGESTED. Largest AI-safety funder by volume and the dominant term in any 2017-2026 series, so its absence is the main coverage gap. The data/raw/funding_sources/open_philanthropy/ scaffold directory name is stale as of Nov 2025. Ingest path is unresolved: Algolia index credentials are published to the browser but reuse terms are unchecked. See #94.
